subject: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@finova.com>, Ben Harper <ben.harper@finova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA follow-up

Thanks again for the call today 

 really appreciate the time. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can land the mutual action plan: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + routing (avg response length ~250 tokens, peak 512 tokens).
- Important decision criteria called out: latency, unit cost, and deployment/SLA options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 + encryption at rest/in transit + audit logs required.

Clarifying questions / asks:
1) Latency target: Can you confirm the P95 target you want for 256-token and 512-token responses? On the call Ben mentioned "sub-200ms" for short responses  is that P50 or P95?
2) Cost threshold: do you have a target blended cost per 1k tokens or a monthly spend budget to hit?
3) Deployment preference: are you leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)? Procurement and security timelines differ significantly.
4) Economic buyer & procurement contacts: who will sign the SOW / PO and who should we loop into contract/security discussions?

Next steps proposed from our side:
- Dev will send a short note on expected P95 latency ranges and SLA options for each deployment mode.
- I’ll send a draft mutual action plan + attachment with deployment options and high-level SLA summary.
- If useful, we can set a 2-week pilot to validate latency/cost on your traffic.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf, redwood-sla-summary.pdf

Thanks  aiming to get this clarified so we can put together a formal quote and MAP.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Harper <ben.harper@finova.com>, Clara Ng <clara.ng@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA follow-up

Hi Marissa 

 thanks for the recap. Helpful. A few answers from our side:

- Latency: Ben and the product team are targeting P95 < 250ms for 256-token outputs and P95 < 400ms for 512-token outputs. They understand tail latency varies by load but those are the thresholds we'll use for procurement decisions.
- Cost: we don't have an exact $/1k-token target, but finance wants a modeled projection for three scenarios (pilot, steady-state 100k req/day, and peak). If you can provide ballpark unit economics by deployment mode that would help.
- Deployment: security has flagged a preference for Dedicated initially (isolated GPU pool) to minimize shared-tenant concerns; Private (VPC) remains on the table if legal requires more control. Procurement wants to understand lead time and any extra compliance costs for Private.
- Stakeholders: Economic buyer is Ben Harper (VP Product). Procurement lead is Clara Ng (contracts@finova.com). Security contact is Rajesh Iyer (rajesh.iyer@finova.com)  please include them on technical & SOC2 questions.

We'd like the mutual action plan next  Procurement will open the SOW & terms once we have an SLA + price band. Also keen to scope a 2-week pilot to validate latency on a small traffic sample.

Thanks  cc'ing Ben and Clara to confirm timeline.

Best,
Aisha
Sr. Product Manager | Finova

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@finova.com>, Ben Harper <ben.harper@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA follow-up

Hi Aisha / Ben 

 quick technical note to set expectations and give the estimates Marissa asked for. High-level takeaways first, details after.

High-level:
- Dedicated: can meet P95 ~120-250ms for 256 tokens and ~200-400ms for 512 tokens depending on model size, batch sizing, and instance class. With a reserved pool sized for steady-state traffic, hitting your targets is realistic. SLA options: 99.9% to 99.95% with SLOs tied to configured capacity.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): equivalent latency is achievable but requires longer procurement & deployment (~6-10 weeks) and extra infra validation. Private lets you maintain KMS/HSM integration and additional audit controls.
- Hosted (shared): lower lead time but tail latency risk at scale; not recommended if procurement requires isolation.

Cost & modelling notes (ballpark):
- Pilot (2 weeks, small pool): estimate $1.5k-9k depending on throughput and model variant.
- Steady-state (100k req/day, avg 250 tokens): projected token spend + reserved capacity ~ $20k-35k/month (depends heavily on batching and KV cache hit rate).
- Peak sizing: add burst capacity costs - we'll model three scenarios in the MAP.

Attachments: I've attached two short docs  redwood-deployment-options.pdf (deployment modes, lead times) and redwood-sla-summary.pdf (SLA tiers, credits, escalation path). I also started a mutual action plan spreadsheet (finova-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with milestones: discovery validation, pilot, procurement, PO/SOW, pilot review, GA rollout.

Pilot logistics suggestion:
- 2-week pilot on Dedicated reserved pool with a conservative capacity buffer. We'll run your traffic subset, collect P95/P99 latency, token usage, and a cost breakdown. We can do this with a token-limited trial account and temporary access keys.

If that aligns, Marissa  can you send the MAP and a preliminary cost band + proposed pilot start dates?

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Regards,
